_comment: Reference strings. To translate: copy this file to <language>.json (e.g. ru.json), translate the values, keep the keys and {placeholders}. Plural entries have forms like one/other; add the forms your language needs (e.g. Russian: one/few/many). Missing entries fall back to English.
plugin.description: Finds the highest-resolution textures in your enabled mods and downscales the ones you choose into a separate output mod.
setting.output_mod_name: Name of the mod that receives downscaled textures
setting.hidden_mods: Mods hidden in the texture list (JSON list)
setting.language: Interface language, e.g. en or ru. Leave empty to use MO2's language. Restart MO2 after changing it.
setting.author_lookup: Look up mod authors on Nexus for the Author column: ask, yes or no
setting.hidden_authors: Authors hidden in the texture list (JSON list)

run_mode.info:
Keep: already downscaled textures are skipped and pre-selected with their previous target.
Rebuild: previous outputs are deleted and everything you select is downscaled again.
authors_prompt.title: Texture Downscaler - mod authors
authors_prompt.text:
Do you want to look up the author of each mod automatically?

MO2 doesn't store mod authors, so the tool would look them up on Nexus Mods. It uses Nexus' public mod information: no account, login or API key is needed, and only the Nexus IDs of your mods ({pages}) are sent. This takes a few seconds once; the results are cached and later only newly installed mods are looked up.

If you choose No, authors show as Unknown. You can still right-click any texture (or the Author column header) and choose Fetch author / Fetch all mod authors at any time. To change the automatic lookup later: MO2 Settings > Plugins > Texture Downscaler > author_lookup.

summary.sizes: |  VRAM if all loaded: {before} -> ~{after} (-{saved})  |  output mod adds ~{after} on disk
summary.tip:
VRAM: a compressed texture takes about as much video memory as its file size. The saving is an upper bound - the game only loads textures for what is around you.
Disk: the original files stay in their mods; the downscaled copies are added to the output mod, so disk usage goes up by the new size.
basic.steps:
1. Select textures in the table (Ctrl / Shift-click, Ctrl+A for all shown).
2. Choose a size and click Mark for downscaling. Marked rows turn blue.
3. Click Downscale marked textures at the bottom. Nothing is written until then.
basic.tips: Tips: double-click a Downscale to cell to change one texture. Right-click rows to hide a mod, deselect a texture type, or filter to a mod/folder. Textures already at or below the chosen size are left alone.
batch.hint: Batch actions apply to all textures currently shown by the filters, not only the selected ones. Use the Mod / Type / search filters or hide mods to narrow them down.
